_comment: wp_wayback — the Wayback Machine endpoints and retry knobs every archive call site goes through. Measured live 2026-09-28, PACED (~1 request/5s per exit). Reliability is ENDPOINT-side, not route-side: /web/timemap/json answered every paced request on every exit tried (median 5-7s); the /web/<ts>id_/<url> redirect resolver every request (<3s; 302 Location = nearest capture, 404 = none); id_ playback every request; /cdx/search/cdx only ~5-6/9 (503 'Temporarily Offline' or a ~40s hang); archive.org/wayback/available 0/27 (always 429, from three unrelated IPs) — dropped from the client. Exits verified reachable: direct (VNPT), Tor (socks5h 127.0.0.1:9050), and the CTI_PROXIES HTTP pool except 37.252.26.70 (407 bad credentials); WARP (socks5h 127.0.0.1:40000) is reachable for HTTP but was NOT hash-verified for snapshot bytes (curl SOCKS failure during the hash run). Snapshot BYTES compared by sha256 direct vs Tor vs one pool proxy MATCH after decompression (id_ replays the capture's original gzip; wp_wayback decompresses centrally). Earlier UNPACED runs overstated proxy failures and got the direct IP firewalled — pace, do not burst.

index._comment: CDX-grammar index endpoints, tried in order on every attempt; a valid empty answer ([]) from any of them is final. timemap/json first (reliable), the classic CDX server second.

playback._comment: Snapshot base: {playback}{timestamp}{modifier}/{original}. id_ = the original bytes (no toolbar/rewrites), if_ = rendered without the toolbar.

latest_timestamp._comment: Placeholder timestamp for 'the newest capture' in the id_ resolver: the archive redirects any timestamp to its nearest real capture.

attempts._comment: Rounds per request. A round tries every index endpoint once; 5xx / timeout / reset / unparseable body move on, 429 and a refused connection stop at once (they arm the egress cooldown in wp_wayback_guard).

backoff_seconds._comment: Sleep before round n+1 = backoff_seconds * n.

truncation_topup_rows._comment: A whole-domain (matchType=domain) index query comes back in URL order, oldest first per URL, so one that fills its row cap silently loses later URLs and recent years (measured: iana.org's 2000 html rows end 2020-05 though captures run to 2026). wayback_ga.cdx_snapshots then merges in this many of the apex's NEWEST html captures (one extra query, negative limit) and flags the result `truncated`.

exits._comment: Default egress routes for the exhaustive archive job (wp_wayback_exhaust / wp_exits), used when env CTI_WAYBACK_EXITS is unset. 'direct' = this machine's IP (archive traffic only — the target is never contacted); 'pool' = every CTI_PROXIES / proxy-store entry; socks5h:// = WARP (127.0.0.1:40000) and Tor (127.0.0.1:9050) as installed on this machine. Each exit is probed once at start; a HARD-broken exit (dead port, 407 credential rejection, SOCKS reply 1/2/4) is dropped for the run and reported, while a merely throttled exit (429) keeps its place and its per-exit cooldown holds it back until it clears. Bytes verified identical across direct / Tor / one pool proxy (sha256); WARP HTTP-reachable but not byte-verified.

exhaust._comment: wp_wayback_exhaust knobs. index_page_rows = rows per paged index request (resumeKey paging); fetch_attempts = tries per capture across exits before it is recorded as failed; exit_fail_limit = consecutive failures after which one exit's worker stops for the run; fetch_timeout = per-request bound in seconds (a failed capture is re-queued to another exit, which is the failover — so the CTI_CALL_TIMEOUT floor is deliberately not applied to these requests); urlscan_page_size / urlscan_max_pages bound the scan listing (a safety ceiling far above any real host — the listing stops when urlscan says has_more=false). urlscan_dom_timeout bounds each /dom/ fetch (seconds, via the unfloored urlopen so one slow DOM cannot stall the run); the DOM pass is resumable (fetched uuids in state), ledgers each DOM to api_usage as it goes, and stops on a 429/402 vendor limit or the run's --max-hours budget, recording the rest as a gap for the next run. default_max_hours = the run budget when --max-hours is not given (analyst setting: 7 h); the MCP tool runs the job DETACHED under this budget, since a synchronous tool call cannot outlive the host's call timeout.

collection_search._comment: Undocumented Wayback collection-search API (verified live 2026-10-03). GET __wb/search/waybacksearch?q=&size=&page=&collection= → {total, hits:[{url,surt_url,host,domain,tld,snippet,title,first_captured,content_type?}]} (empty may be []); GET __wb/search/collectioninfo?collection= → {count,last_updated,description,collection,title,url} or {} when unknown. Latency 13–50s → timeout ≥60s. A collection that returns {} or errors is reported as unavailable, NEVER as empty. telegram → telegram.username kit rows; pdf → host kit rows; mediacloud/russian-independent-media/EoT → mention_only facts. RULE 1: no case data.
